tasks.short: Fit nutrition plans to individual preferences

steps.what: Explore cultural, ethnic and religious preferences with the patient
Incorporate preferences into clinically suitable nutrition plans

tasks.design: Keep the personal conversation and clinical adaptation with the dietitian. The {DOCS} plan records what this patient wants rather than inferring preferences from group membership.
tasks.previous_blocker: Individual preferences and clinical tradeoffs cannot be reduced to a cultural label.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing document tools support recording the agreed plan; no new capability is assumed.
tasks.still_hard: Reconciling nutritional needs, affordability and personal practice.
tasks.human_edge: Ask without stereotyping and negotiate an acceptable plan.
tasks.altitude: Decision rights and patient time remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Individual preference elicitation and clinical adaptation remain professional work in this proposed boundary; no saving is evidenced.

assumptions: Boundary includes dietitian conversation and plan adaptation, not patient cooking or a separate recipe-development task.
The dietitian produces the individual preferences in s1; no structured flags or machine actions are assumed.
Use existing document configuration first. No new automation or upkeep is introduced, so incremental upkeep is zero.
research_questions: Does the patient recognise their own preferences in the final plan?

incremental.description: No changed service or software to maintain

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, incremental=0, net=0. Personal preference discussion and adaptation retain all time; no documentation saving is assumed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Agree nutritional needs with care colleagues

steps.what: Consult care personnel about nutritional needs and diet restrictions

tasks.design: Keep consultation and resolution of conflicting requirements with the care team. Existing {DOCS} records remain supporting inputs; no shorter conversation is claimed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Colleagues must reconcile incomplete information and competing treatment goals.
tasks.enabler_now: No new capability is needed for the retained consultation.
tasks.still_hard: Resolving uncertainty about restrictions without delaying care.
tasks.human_edge: Question assumptions and negotiate a shared clinical interpretation.
tasks.altitude: The dietitian retains the same advisory authority.

reach.learn: Clarify when observations change dietary advice

evidence.claim: Consultation requires clinical interpretation; this design makes no evidence-backed reduction in its duration.

assumptions: Only dietitian consultation time is counted; colleague time is outside the focal denominator and remains unchanged.
Care personnel produce their assessments under existing care processes; no machine-ready restrictions are assumed or consumed.
Check native record access before adding tools. Unchanged consultation requires zero incremental upkeep.
research_questions: Which unresolved clinical questions require direct colleague discussion?

incremental.description: No additional workflow or model upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. The consultation remains intact even when electronic records are available.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Elicit patient and family health and food history
Record the elicited history in the clinical record

loop.input: Consented consultation account or dietitian dictation
loop.output: Draft history note with uncertain facts marked
loop.check: Dietitian checks symptoms, exposures, allergies, medicines, chronology, attribution and omissions against the source
loop.stop: One draft; incomplete or ambiguous input returns to manual documentation
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative history cannot be faithfully captured by fixed field copying alone

steps.what: Evaluate history and confirm the final clinical record

tasks.design: An {OTHER} clinical record system holds a draft derived from the consultation or dictation. The dietitian checks its meaning, evaluates the history and confirms the exact final record; consultation and clinical assessment retain their time.
tasks.previous_blocker: Narrative capture requires wording as well as factual checking.
tasks.enabler_now: Clinical note drafting with clinician validation exists; transfer to this speciality remains a local test.
tasks.still_hard: Detecting omitted exposures or misattributed family conditions.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise clinically significant details and ask follow-up questions.
tasks.altitude: Less initial wording, with unchanged clinical responsibility.

reach.learn: Audit source attribution and missing information

evidence.claim: Autoscriber drafts consultation records with clinician validation; this supports the documentation pattern, not dietitian-specific savings.
The proposed 40% reduction in initial recording effort is an unmeasured scenario and does not shorten history taking or evaluation.

assumptions: Boundary is dietitian history taking, recording and evaluation; do not add these steps again to another consultation estimate.

The dietitian produces history content during s1, including symptoms, exposures, allergies, medicines, family attribution and preventive measures. Source capture and clarification stay within its full 55 hours; no free structured fields are assumed.
Test native dictation and note templates before custom integration. Without permitted recording use counted dietitian dictation or manual notes.
Three additional focal hours cover source audits, template corrections and failed draft handling.
unknowns: Actual documentation share and editing effort
research_questions: Does source-checked drafting reduce net recording time without losing clinically important history?

already_counted.description: Clinical evaluation and exact record confirmation

incremental.description: Source audits, template upkeep and exceptional draft failures

approvals.approved_version: Exact final history note, patient identity, source attribution and clinical interpretation; any edit requires renewed confirmation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=55+15+20=90, gross=10, upkeep=3, central net=7. Low: all initial recording time remains and upkeep still costs 3; high: 40% of the 25-hour recording component is saved. Clinical contact and evaluation never shrink.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop menus for special nutritional needs

steps.what: Define special nutrition requirements and verify available ingredient information
Develop candidate recipes and menus against the brief

loop.purpose: Draft menu combinations from verified recipes
loop.input: Dietitian brief, verified ingredient information and approved recipe library
loop.output: Candidate menus with recipe references and unresolved constraints
loop.check: Dietitian verifies every ingredient, substitution, portion, nutrient calculation and restriction against authoritative specifications
loop.stop: One candidate set; missing allergen or suitability evidence returns to manual development
loop.why_not_simpler: Combining acceptable meals involves contextual variety and preference beyond numeric filtering

steps.what: Validate recipes and menus for nutritional suitability and practical use

tasks.design: The {DOCS} recipe library supplies referenced candidates, with deterministic nutrient arithmetic where verified quantities exist and a bounded loop for menu wording and combinations. The dietitian retains requirement capture, ingredient verification, practical checks and approval before use.
tasks.previous_blocker: Producing varied options requires assembling recipes while respecting individual constraints.
tasks.enabler_now: Constrained drafting and arithmetic are plausible building blocks, without validated speciality performance in this digest.
tasks.still_hard: Incomplete ingredient declarations, substitutions and clinically unsuitable combinations.
tasks.human_edge: Judge whether a nutritionally adequate menu is safe, acceptable and practical.
tasks.altitude: The dietitian spends less time composing candidates while retaining all release decisions.

reach.task: Check preparation matches the approved menu
reach.learn: Trace substitutions back to verified ingredient specifications

evidence.claim: A constrained menu drafting aid is plausible model knowledge; the digest does not validate special-diet recipe generation or its safety.

assumptions: Boundary includes dietitian development and validation, excluding cooking and the separate patient preference interview.

The dietitian produces s1's menu brief with restrictions, targets, portion units and preferences and verifies ingredient, allergen and nutrient source versions. All capture and missing-data clarification retain s1's 25 hours; unverified fields force manual development.
Test native recipe templates and nutrient calculations first. Drafting cannot infer allergen absence or turn a missing declaration into a safe ingredient.
An existing approved recipe library is required; additional focal upkeep of 4 hours and food-service specification upkeep of 2 hours are counted.
unknowns: Availability and currency of verified recipe and ingredient data
Actual effort spent composing rather than testing
research_questions: Can candidate drafting save composition time after ingredient and clinical checks?

incremental.description: Dietitian recipe constraints and source audits

approvals.approved_version: Exact menu, recipe and ingredient versions, portions, restrictions and nutrient calculations; substitutions void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=25+24+35=84, gross=16, focal upkeep=4, central net=12. High assumes verified reusable recipes and a 40% reduction of candidate composition only; low retains all composition effort plus upkeep when sources are incomplete. Food-service upkeep is disclosed separately.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Clinical judgement, collaboration and individual adaptation remain central; selected drafting may shorten paperwork and candidate composition.
reach: Work with dietetic technicians on ingredient traceability
Work with medical records specialists on faithful history capture
role.ambitious_version: A dietitian with clearer records and traceable menu proposals, while retaining personal care and nutritional decisions.
